lessons.title: Transactional schema changes and returned writes
lessons.intro:
SQLite 3.35+; every question starts with a fresh in-memory database; result order is specified when relevant. A schema change alters contracts that application queries depend on. SQLite supports transactional DDL, so a migration can group related changes and roll back on failure. Use explicit column names when inserting to avoid depending on table order. RETURNING exposes values from changed rows in SQLite 3.35 and later, but does not imply the surrounding transaction is committed. Savepoints provide nested rollback boundaries; releasing one is not necessarily a top-level commit.
